source_title: Iran war live: Araghchi says talks under way on 2-day plan to reopen Hormuz
source_excerpt: ‘Epic resilience’ by Iran’s military has brought the US and allies to the ‘hard wall of reality’ over the conflict, official says. Iran FM Araghchi calls US dialogue offer ‘a positive step’ as Iranian delegation visits Doha Iran warns it can inflict “devastating strikes” on US warships in the Middle East and says enemy forces attempting a ground invasion will face a “killing ground”. US President Donald Trump says negotiations with Iran are “going fine”, but he is “not in that much of a hurry” to make a peace deal. Iran warns it can inflict “devastating strikes” on US warships in the Middle East and says enemy forces attempting a ground invasion will face a “killing ground”. US President Donald Trump says negotiations with Iran are “going fine”, but he is “not in that much of a hurry” to make a peace deal. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks are ongoing with Qatari mediators on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US cooperates. Tehran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, says a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance changed the US tone “completely”, describing it as a “very positive sign”. live-orange 5m ago ( 22:30 GMT ) Yemen’s foreign minister demands accountability for UN worker death in Houthi custody Yemen’s Foreign Minister Afrah Al-Zouba has called for the Houthis to be held accountable for the death of UN High Commissioner for Human Rights employee, Mohammed Ibrahim al-Shami, who was detained by the armed group in Yemen for more than two years. In a post on X, Al-Zouba said the “horrific crime for which the militia bears full responsibility” necessitated decisive international action to hold the perpetrators accountable. “His tragedy did not begin with his death; it began with his abduction in June 2024, his enforced disappearance, and the deprivation of his family from communicating with him or knowing his fate,” she said. Al-Zouba called for the United Nations and the UN Security Council to take action to force the Houthis to release all “abductees”. In a statement posted on X, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the attack as a serious threat to maritime safety and global energy supplies. It warned that the incident could have dangerous consequences for the marine environment and regional security. Yet, agreements to stop war matter most when distrust is the deepest. The key question is whether regional governments can agree on rules that make their disagreements less destructive. In a recent lecture at Cambridge University in the UK, Oman’s Foreign Minister, Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, called for a non-aggression pact among all eight Gulf littoral states: the six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council along with Iraq and Iran. He described it as the essential prerequisite for an inclusive regional security architecture. Could such a pact work? As Albusaidi conceded, it would be hard to achieve. But as another major escalation looms between Iran and the United States, the region urgently needs a diplomatic path forward. Indeed, the ongoing conflict has proved so hard to resolve because the region’s security arrangements have remained underdeveloped, relying for too long on external powers. The way forward, then, can be an inclusive agreement. Read more here . Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi with Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi in Tehran, August 25, 2026. The claim of the IRGC’s public relations office was circulated by Iran’s state news agency IRNA among others. The IRGC said the vessels had been using an “unauthorised route” through the strait, a route Iran claims authority over and that is not recognised under international law. It claimed the tankers had turned off their navigation and identification systems and were trying to pass in secret with the support of the US military, but stopped in place after the explosions. The statement did not name the ships or mention any injuries or casualties. Bahrain termed the attack as a grave threat to maritime safety, marine environments, and global energy supply security, as well as a breach of international law and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. In a statement, the Bahraini Ministry of Foreign Affairs reaffirmed Bahrain’s full solidarity with Qatar and support for all measures taken to safeguard its security, vital interests, vessels, and crews. The Ministry called on the international community, particularly the UN Security Council, to take decisive action to prevent recurring attacks, hold perpetrators accountable, and guarantee freedom of navigation and safe transit through international waterways, in a manner that ensures energy security and the flow of global trade, and promotes security, stability, and sustainable development in the region and the world. But even amid signs of diplomatic progress, officials from both sides say they are ready for renewed military escalation . President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly suggested the United States could attack Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, said the latest negotiations were “going fine”, but added that the US still had several Iranian targets to “take care of”. Meanwhile, Araghchi has also said Iran’s military was more prepared than ever for renewed war, while the country’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, threatened Iran would use “new weaponry” in response to any future attack.
